# Oxford Learner's Dictionaries

> > Comprehensive English language learning dictionaries from Oxford University Press, featuring the Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary (OALD) with detailed definitions, pronunciations, usage notes, and etymology.

Oxford Learner's Dictionaries provides authoritative English language resources for learners worldwide, including the Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary, Oxford Advanced American Dictionary, Oxford Collocations Dictionary, and specialized tools like the Text Checker. Each entry includes pronunciation guides, usage examples, word origins (often from Latin, Old French, and Greek), and OPAL (Oxford Phrasal Academic Lexicon) indicators for academic vocabulary.

## Key Topics

- Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary (OALD)
- English vocabulary and definitions
- Pronunciation guides
- OPAL (Oxford Phrasal Academic Lexicon)
- Etymology and word origins
- Usage notes and examples
- Oxford Collocations Dictionary
- Practical English Usage
- Text Checker tool
- British and American English
- Academic and formal vocabulary
- Part of speech classifications
- Oxford University Press
- Language learning resources

## Learning Tools & Resources

- [Text Checker](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/text-checker/index.html): Text Checker tool for writing assistance and language verification
- [Oxford Student's Dictionary](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/about/students.html): Oxford Student's Dictionary with interactive resources and videos

## Core Vocabulary - OPAL Words

- [access (noun)](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/access_1): OPAL word 'access' noun with comprehensive usage examples
- [accountability (noun)](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/accountability): OPAL formal vocabulary: 'accountability' noun definition
- [abnormal (adjective)](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/abnormal): OPAL word 'abnormal' adjective definition with usage examples

- [abominate (verb)](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/abominate): Formal verb 'abominate' with Latin etymology and usage notes
- [abrogation (noun)](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/abrogation): Formal legal term 'abrogation' noun definition and usage
- [abashed (adjective)](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/abashed): Etymology-rich entry for 'abashed' from Middle English and French
- [acolyte (noun)](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/acolyte): Dictionary entry for 'acolyte' with etymology from Latin and Old French
